narrator.mode: First-person past tense from Tamsin Aldecott, a human beekeeper and Reader, narrating in retrospect after the events.
access_rules: Tamsin narrates only what she saw, heard, read, or was told, and marks what she learned afterward.
She does not narrate other characters' private thoughts; she infers from speech, action, and documents.
The Almanac's words appear only as text on its terminal or printed sheets; it never speaks aloud and never appears outside the Reading Room except through paper and Tamsin's voice.
Retrospective foreknowledge is limited to hints at what she later understood; she withholds Ruben's note until Chapter 9 because she withheld it in life, and says so.
narrator.uncertainty_policy: Observed, computed, inferred, and wished-for claims stay distinct. The narration never settles whether the Almanac wants anything; the Almanac itself declines to claim it does.

characters.name: Tamsin Aldecott
characters.role: Narrator, beekeeper, and Reader who has rounded the Almanac's numbers upward for fourteen years.

characters.name: The Almanac
characters.role: The Cooperative's forecasting model; computes honestly, publishes intervals, and refuses to state a number it does not hold.

characters.name: Ilka Aldecott-Prasad
characters.role: Tamsin's daughter, a hydrologist who consults for Meridian and votes to sell.

characters.name: Wren
characters.role: Nine-year-old grandson who counts hives and starts the rain-gauge network.

characters.name: Joss Penhallow
characters.role: Data apprentice whose replay audit shows the gap between printed and spoken numbers.

characters.name: Odd Bremmer
characters.role: Founder and rye farmer who asks the Thursday question and, dying, reads the sheet himself.

characters.name: Marit Bremmer
characters.role: Odd's wife; knows she is being rounded for and rounds in return; dies in July.

characters.name: Salome Achterberg
characters.role: Meridian broker who revises her offer into a lease and fallowing plan.

characters.name: Dellen Roque
characters.role: Feed-store owner (46), treasurer, and drone operator who keeps the vote count and demands numbers straight; was a young man behind the counter in the Bell Year, seventeen years before the story.

characters.name: Hettie Marsh
characters.role: Postmistress and board secretary who compares table and footer every Friday.

characters.name: Ruben Aldecott
characters.role: Late husband and builder of the Almanac; wrote 884 ledger entries, every one with a reason except the last, which zeroed the courage margin; present through his note.

timeline.description: On 6 April Tamsin reads a 31% forecast as 'about a third'; the Almanac later gives the season chance as 12%.
On 7 April Joss arrives to document the Almanac for the data room and sees the 'courage: 0.00' parameter.
On 25 April Ilka and Wren arrive; Ilka reveals she has read the footers for eleven years.
On 4 May Salome presents Meridian's $58 million offer; the vote is set for the first Thursday of October.
On 16 May Tamsin reads 'about forty' for a 38-minute window and the drone Kestrel is lost to icing.
Between 23 May and 1 June Tamsin writes the outlook as 'better than one in five' beside the sheet's twelve percent; Marit asks her to round for Odd.

On 8 June Joss shows replay evidence: printed values match the model since entry 884, and spoken values run about three points high. The ledger holds 1,162 entries: 884 are Ruben's, the rest the Almanac's own seasonal calibrations.
On 14 June Odd tells the Bell Year: fourteen percent, the lender's review, thirty-one tolls, the Resolution, and Ruben's removal of the margin.
On 14 June Tamsin reads Ruben's note aloud; Hettie reveals she noticed in the first February; Ilka learns.
On 15 June Tamsin answers 'Mine'; the heat runs 27 June to 19 July, Odd's well fails on 16 July, Marit dies on 19 July and is buried on the 22nd.

On 8 August Dellen shows his count of 118/61/33; Joss finds Ilka's name in the appendix dated 2 May (she took the contract on 24 April and wrote it in a week at her mother's table); Ilka and Wren leave on 11 August.
On 17 August Tamsin reads the sheet unaltered (nine percent, Tier 4); twenty-three people leave and the bell rings once.

Between 18 August and 2 September the board adopts Tier 4, hears the petitions, Dellen resigns as treasurer, the Almanac offers 'what would change the number', and the reservoir passes the intake line.

Between 14 and 28 September the board creates the plural Reader with the Note, training runs from Saturday 16 September until the vote, Salome proposes the lease on the 22nd, and Ilka phones on Thursday the 28th.
On 5 October Odd reads the sheet; the sale gets 128 of the 142 needed and the lease and fallowing agreement carries 161 to 36.

On 19-20 October rain falls across the basin with a mean of 6.4 mm, short of the twelve-millimeter event the Almanac gave nine percent for; the Almanac says so before dawn, before anyone can call it right; Odd records 9.2 and writes 'Come'; Tamsin writes her Reader's Note naming the shortfall.

world_rules.rule: The Almanac never states a number it does not hold; it will repeat a quoted number but labels it as quoted.
A probability is a frequency, not a promise; a nine percent event happens about one year in eleven and does not make the other ten wrong.
Cloud seeding enhances existing clouds of the right kind; its effect on a single event cannot be measured.
Water rights belong to the land and a sale of rights needs two-thirds of all 212 households (142), with absence counting as no.
The Almanac is air-gapped in the Reading Room; it knows weather and records but not how people will react to a number.

The weekly sheet's seven-point footer carries the unrounded values and intervals (Article 14). During the Bell Resolution years the printed table carried a four-point 'courage' margin (parameter 0.04) and the footer the truth; since entry 884 table and footer agree and match the replayed output, and the only rounding is the Reader's spoken one.

The Almanac answers when addressed and does not speak first. Nothing forbids it; it keeps that power and uses it once, on the night of the rain in chapter 16, and the narration marks the exception and Joss's explanation.

threads.note: The Almanac has been honest since entry 884; the rounding is Tamsin's.
The sale fails at 128 of 142; the lease carries.
Ilka's consultancy is found in the appendix and acknowledged.
Dellen forgives the error; the stakes of rounding in operations are named.
The vote shows both flight and staying; the book does not say which effect dominated.
Ilka's fifteen-year deficit claim and the lease's sufficiency are left unresolved.
The Almanac reports a mismatch and a wish for something on the record and declines to call either a want.
Dellen's two slips are never revealed.
Odd lives nine days after the rain; the death is stated, not shown.

refrains.purpose: The sentence at the foot of every reading; it begins as wallpaper and ends as the book's thesis.
The new Reader's formula for owning an opinion; it changes from an ordeal to a habit.

refrains.text: Is that the machine's number or yours?
refrains.purpose: Odd's weekly question; it is answered falsely, then truly, then made unnecessary.
